results.question: Who won the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix? I'd like the winner's forename and surname, the local clock time (hours:minutes:seconds.milliseconds) at the circuit at which he crossed the finish line, and the url of his information page, so I can compare the moment the race ended with the TV coverage.
results.evidence: A driver's race time is the duration from the start of the race to the moment he crosses the finish line.
results.sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, time(r.time, '0' || res.time) || '.' || substr(res.time, -3) AS finish_time, d.url FROM races r JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = res.driverId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Azerbaijan Grand Prix' AND res.positionOrder = 1
results.predicted_sql:
SELECT r.raceId, r.year, r.name AS race, r.date, r.time AS start_time, r.url AS race_url,
       c.name AS circuit, c.location, c.country,
       d.forename, d.surname, d.url AS driver_url,
       res.time AS race_time, res.milliseconds, res.positionOrder
FROM races r
JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId
JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = res.driverId
WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name LIKE '%Azerbaijan%' AND res.positionOrder = 1;

results.question: I'm preparing a department audit on how often anti-ribonuclear protein testing comes back clearly elevated among the women in the thrombosis cohort. Among the women in the cohort, what percentage of those with an available anti-ribonuclear protein test result had a clearly elevated result? Please give me the percentage rounded to two decimal places on the 0-100 scale. Note: elevated means a titer strictly above 1:64. Patients never tested for anti-ribonuclear protein should be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, while a negative reading counts as an available result and is never elevated.
results.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein is a serology test reported as a titer reading; a negative reading is a result of zero titer.
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L WHERE L.ID = P.ID AND CAST(L.RNP AS REAL) > 64) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM Patient P WHERE P.SEX = 'F' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L WHERE L.ID = P.ID AND L.RNP IS NOT NULL)
results.predicted_sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.ID FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.RNP IS NOT NULL
